_meta.alcance: Documentary synthesis explaining the team’s proposals; not a rotation trial or validation of engine parameters.
_meta.nota_comun: Engine values for water, nitrogen, ground cover and income remain team estimates pending local validation. Harvests, fertilizer savings and profitability are not guaranteed.
vacios_comunes: Soil tests, irrigation, varieties, pests and costs for this plot are unknown.
Agronomic sources explain general mechanisms; they do not establish which of these three sequences is best at the selected point.

fuentes.titulo: Development of a Framework for Good Agricultural Practices (2003)
fuentes.alcance: Supports ground cover, residue recycling and the inclusion of legumes. Does not assess these sequences in Cajamarca.

fuentes.titulo: Irrigation Water Management: Crop Water Needs, chapter 3
fuentes.alcance: Water needs depend on climate, crop and growth stage; the ranges are guidance, not local calibration.
Supports the potential of faba bean as green manure to supply nitrogen and organic matter. Management in Chile does not validate calendars or application rates for Peru.

fuentes.titulo: Manejo de pastos asociados anuales para la alimentación de ganado lechero (2021)
fuentes.seccion: Abstract of the institutional repository record
fuentes.alcance: Describes oats, vetch and peas grown together for highland livestock. Does not test rotation B or establish its profitability.

fuentes.seccion: Notes: KILLING T and FURTHER INF
fuentes.alcance: Supports nitrogen fixation and warns that young plants are sensitive to frost and excess moisture. Does not demonstrate water savings relative to rotation A.

fuentes.titulo: Tecnología de producción de semilla de vicia forrajera (2013)
fuentes.seccion: Abstract of the institutional repository record
fuentes.alcance: Identifies Vicia sativa as a forage legume used in Junín. Does not validate sequence C across the highlands.

fichas.por_que: A reference for comparing the team’s proposal with alternatives that include legumes and forage. The name Traditional does not imply that its use has been verified in every community.

beneficios.texto: Alternating species helps plan nutrient and crop health management; benefits depend on the crops and how they are managed.

limites: This sequence has no cultivated nitrogen-fixing legume. Fallow alone does not guarantee fertility recovery.
If land is left bare during fallow, rainfall can remove soil; actual ground cover needs to be checked.
The water score compares estimated demand per planted growing season: a year without a harvest is not counted as water savings.
revisar: What is actually grown on the plot, and which crop health problems recur?
Are ground cover and residues maintained during fallow?
Is there enough water for potato and maize during sensitive growth stages?

fichas.secuencia: Potato → Faba bean → Barley → Forage oats
fichas.por_que: An option to explore when soil care and livestock feed are priorities. Its ranking depends on the climate and your priorities.

beneficios.texto: Faba bean can fix nitrogen through its association with bacteria. What remains for the next crop depends on residues returned to the soil and material removed at harvest.
Oats offer a documented forage option in highland livestock systems. This does not guarantee higher milk production or income.

limites: Evidence for faba bean as green manure does not imply the same nitrogen contribution when it is harvested for grain.
Removing all forage can reduce the residues that protect the soil.
Faba bean suitability as animal feed needs review: the model assigns forage value, but the consulted INIA Chile source does not recommend that use in its context.
revisar: Will faba bean be harvested for grain or managed as green manure?
What share of residues will remain on the land?
Which oat and barley varieties suit the location, and when should they be cut?

fichas.secuencia: Potato → Andean lupin (tarwi) → Wheat → Common vetch
fichas.por_que: Explores a combination of two legumes and a forage species. Water efficient names a model alternative; lower water use on the plot has not yet been demonstrated.

beneficios.texto: Andean lupin can fix nitrogen; the amount available to other crops depends on management and soil conditions.
Vetch is used as a forage legume in the highlands. Maintaining ground cover and residues can help protect soil from erosion.

limites: There is no local validation that this full sequence saves water compared with the other two. Lower demand comes from estimated team parameters.
Young Andean lupin plants may be sensitive to frost, and the crop to excess moisture; it should not be presented as resilient under all conditions.
Cutting and removing vetch as forage changes residue and nutrient inputs compared with leaving it as ground cover or green manure.
revisar: Are locally adapted Andean lupin and vetch seeds available?
Does the land drain well, and which growth stages coincide with frost months?
Will vetch be removed as forage or returned to the soil?
